Definition: Assuming someone is wrong, then explaining psychologically why they believe it, instead of showing the error. Motives do not settle truth, even when the motives are correctly described.
Example: Someone argues, 'You only oppose this policy because you fear change.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'You only believe in God because you need a crutch.'
HowToRespond: Return to reasons: 'Even if motives were as claimed, motives don't settle truth — let's examine the reasons.'
